iem-cca-cst.review: A single DD with a nice tuning for a piston-shaped earphone like this, compared with cheap Sonys. If you don't like over-ear-hook style earphones, this could be your answer. Really nice, very similar to the Sony MH755, honestly. The driver is genuinely good and the tuning pleasant; it can compete with the Final E1000. Annoyingly, the cable can't be replaced; I'll try whether it can be recabled or made detachable. But sound-quality-wise it's nice, and it could make a birthday gift since the design is really attractive.

iem-moondrop-stellaris.review: As much as I dislike Moondrop, I still really respect the Blessing 2, Aria, Starfield, KXXS and Kanas Pro. But this is weird. Don't buy it. The mid-lows are odd and the treble is way overdone. No. Just skip it. Better the Starfield or Kato if you want to stay with Moondrop; I'd still take the Olina SE or Tangzu Zetian.

iem-7hz-salnotes-dioko-x-crinacle.review: Good technicalities, but the bass tuning isn't great, and it's too bright for me. Sorry, I'm just not Team Crinacle tuning; I'm Team BGGAR. If I want to feel the bass I'll surely raise the volume until I get it, but my ears get stabbed by the treble first.

iem-kinera-wyvern-abyss-ungu.review: Who knows which TikTok creator made this viral. It's super muffled compared with the white one. If you want a Kinera, get the white one: a far better, very mature tuning, balanced with a little warmth, and good imaging, not veiled like this. Very covered, muffled.

iem-ak6-pro.review: Value for money, bro; great for people on a minimal budget. But if you have the budget, I'd at least go for the TRN MT1, hehe. Still, I'm glad ChiFi has cheap things that aren't bad. Build quality may be fragile. The nice thing about this one is you can change the cable.

headphone-wireless-sony-wh-1000xm6.review: The perfect lifestyle wireless headphone. World-class ANC, superb vocal timbre. A 10-band EQ, flexible to set the tonality you want, on a base that's already balanced, with a bit much low-mid around 100–200 Hz. The best vocal timbre I've heard on a wireless headphone, with smooth, velvety highs. The bass isn't as much as the Momentum 4. ANC better than the QC Ultra. Unmatched microphone quality compared with other brands. Really. The best wireless headphone so far, as a wireless (not as a wired). Main weakness: no wired mode over USB-C, though you can use it while charging with Bluetooth on.

headphone-wireless-jbl-tour-one-m3.tagline: Superb fit; finally good-sounding portable audio from JBL
headphone-wireless-jbl-tour-one-m3.review: I've only tried it twice, at JBL Fest and while shooting the best wireless headphones of 2025 at Jagat Review, but the tuning is completely sorted and so is the driver. It can definitely compete with the XM6 and really beats Bose. Natural mids and timbre, upper mids to treble that aren't sharp, well balanced. The earcups are roomy like Bose's. Shame I don't have a review unit. The bass isn't as much as the Sennheiser Momentum 4, with better earpads too. Very good: probably the best portable audio from JBL, not their TWS or speakers but this headphone. And its price competes with other top-tier wireless headphones.

headphone-wireless-sennheiser-hdb-630.review: The tuning is even more accurate and natural, with less sub than the Momentum. A missed opportunity: it comes with a dongle, but not a 2.4 GHz gaming one; instead a Bluetooth transmitter for aptX Lossless. A shame, half-baked. Clean mid-bass, superb punch, clarity and separation. The earpads aren't as roomy as JBL or Bose. And my rule still stands: A PRICE ABOVE AIRPODS IS FORBIDDEN. Brands like this have to price below the AirPods Max, or they'll struggle to sell, mate.

headphone-wireless-bose-quietcomfort-2nd.tagline: Proper ANC with a superb fit
headphone-wireless-bose-quietcomfort-2nd.review: A nice fit, close to the Ultra. The ANC is world-class too, about Sony's level. It has a USB-C cable mode for lossless audio, and a C-to-3.5 mm cable is included. I actually prefer this default tonality to the Ultra, which is a bit more V-shaped, though the highs are a little less well defined than the Ultra, and the Ultra's soundstage is slightly grander. The mic can't match Sony yet. (The rest is in his video.)

headphone-wireless-sennheiser-momentum-4.review: A top-class, best-sounding high-end headphone, suited to people who still want bass. Not neutral like the Stax S3. Its quality is already like a wired closed-back. Lovely, clear microphone, not far from the XM5; the XM5 wins with a lot of wind or in a café, but the Momentum 4 isn't far behind. The FRAUNHOFER SOUND PERSONALISATION IS EXCELLENT!

headphone-wireless-bose-quietcomfort-ult.review: UNRIVALLED NOISE-CANCELLING HEADPHONES, but overpriced. The sound is balanced, leaning a bit bassy, but EQable. Sennheiser can actually match it on sound alone. The ANC and transparency are truly superb. Maybe at around 4 million rupiah it'd be humane, but at a 5-million budget I'd rather take the Momentum 4 at around 4 million, unless you really want super-amazing noise cancelling. Sound, fit and ANC are above the XM5. (Video review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-fiio-eh13.review: Best sound. The app is still a bit buggy; hopefully a firmware update comes. But once you've settled on your own EQ or another user's (mine included), I think this is the best-sounding: an OK, fun sub-bass extension, clear mids, more powerful volume. Literally the best compared with EarFun, Edifier and Tozo in terms of sound. The mic is OK too. Only the ANC isn't great. (Review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-sony-wh-1000xm5.review: Good overall at an attractive price. Good mic; on the street or in a café the noise reduction gets a bit strong, so it turns robotic. The driver isn't as good as Sennheiser's, though Sony's driver is still OK. It loses badly on battery. ANC + mic are the best. Comfortable. Not for sports. SPOTIFY TAP: an integrated Spotify feature that doesn't just skip songs but switches playlists straight from what you usually listen to.

headphone-wireless-sony-wh-ch730n.review: Now this is great: an upgrade over the weak 720. The sound is more or less the same as the ULT Wear, but cheaper. The clamp is a bit tighter than the ULT Wear, but still comfortable, and the earpads are still roomy. A good mic, about 75% of the XM6's quality. ANC is OK. Launch price 1.7 million, while the ULT Wear is too basshead at 2.1 down to 1.8 million. So just buy this. (Review and EQ on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-sony-ult-wear.review: You should skip the CH720 and come here. It easily covers a wide audience, especially those who like BASS! Three modes: ULT Off (warm-balanced), ULT 1 (a bass boost I can still enjoy), ULT 2 (overdone, distorted bass). Stay on Off or 1. ANC, mic and fit are better than the Accentum, but I prefer the Accentum's sound (I like clear mids and just don't like basshead). Folds, comes with a case. (Review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-sennheiser.review: Great mids, punch, well balanced. Better than the XM5 in terms of sound. The ANC is serious too, good, not a token or fake one like cheap wireless headphones. The cups are a bit smaller than the M4, but they still go around my ears, though fairly snugly. Custom EQ. Done. It can also run wired over USB-C! CHARGE AND USE!

headphone-wireless-edifier-stax-s3.review: THE BEST NEUTRAL-SOUNDING WIRELESS HEADPHONE. Superb technicalities. I love this more than the Sennheiser Momentum 4, because of the planar driver and its lovely neutral tuning. Neutral doesn't mean no bass. It really lets you hear the music as the engineer intended. Smooth, forward vocals, with reverb echoes and tails and snare vibration all audible, every detail clear. Fast bass. Its only lack is ANC, but I'm fine. No EQ either, but this is already the sound I like most. Comes with 2 great earpads; the leather ones are bassier, I use the Ice ones, which are cooler and more comfortable. If you're not a neutral audiophile it may not suit you; the Sennheiser Accentum may suit you better.

headphone-wireless-tozo-h20.review: Good. Wider and more spacious than the H10. The treble emphasis is still there but doesn't bother; that's just the H20's character. The Tune Pro is brighter in the upper mids/lower treble; this is airier. It has LDAC. Replacement earpads are available from Tozo. (Full review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-earfun-tune-pro.review: Basically a Wave Pro + Space Pro. More bass than the Wave Pro, technically almost the same. Not too neutral, and not as boomy as the Space Pro. 2-year warranty, comes with a case, cheaper than the Space Pro. The best ANC too, in quietness and the comfort of the ANC algorithm. Minus: the fit isn't as roomy as the Wave Pro.

headphone-wireless-earfun-wave-pro.review: KING OF UNDER 1 MILLION RUPIAH. Not a basshead tuning: verrry well balanced, midrange-centric. I cut its mids and treble to be more balanced (see the EQ section). ANC, transparency, 55 ms game mode, LDAC, multipoint, up to 80 hours of battery. A nice fit, and a case like Sony's. CRAZY! (Video review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-fiio-eh11.review: The best-sounding on-ear: the Sony CH520 loses, the JLab Rewind loses. Against the Moondrop Old Fashioned and Koss KPH40 it competes very well too, since it takes a parametric EQ, which is excellent: I could boost the bass more and cut the slightly airy treble. Weak on the mic, and the drivers can't swivel. Otherwise mostly positive.

headphone-wireless-edifier-w830nb.review: More open, more spacious. The sound is maybe nearly identical to the Wave Pro, but the ANC and transparency here are tidier. A more minimalist style too, no logo. It doesn't come with extra earpads like the Wave Pro. The battery is great, and there's a USB-C WIRED mode: it shows up as a DAC output and mic input on a laptop/phone, while charging. Just buy this; skip the W950NB. (Full review on his YouTube: WH700NB Pro vs W800BT Pro vs W830NB.)

headphone-wireless-tozo-h10.review: I'd much rather have this than LDAC with a tiny EQ like the Space Pro's. It has a 10-band custom EQ. Technicalities and tonality can rival the Space Pro. It's also much louder than Edifier and EarFun. A very good one from Tozo. (Comparison in his video.)

headphone-wireless-soundpeats-space-pro.review: The best driver at 600k right now! Champion technicalities: separation, wide imaging, compared with the W800BT Pro. The highs are better in LDAC mode too; in AAC mode it's very compressed. One of the wireless headphones where AAC and LDAC are worlds apart. Has a USB-C wired mode. 150-hour battery! (Review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-earfun-wave-life.review: This, the W800BT Pro and the Space Pro are all the same class; this one's tuning is just more bass-heavy: the deepest, fat, round and fun. It's down to which you prefer, and you can still reduce it; that's simply the driver's character. The W800BT Pro will never be this bass-heavy whatever you do, and neither will the Space Pro. (Review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-edifier-stax-s5.review: The sound is tidier than the S3: a cleaner midrange and a wider soundstage. But it's still the same: the volume is a bit low, and it now has a USB-C mode too. Still no ANC. And the price, oh my.

headphone-wireless-bower-wilkins.review: The driver isn't bad, but sadly it lacks a lot in features and battery, and the EQ is very limited: only bass and treble, and I'm not sure at which frequencies. Better buy Sony or Sennheiser: good sound without sacrificing features.

headphone-wireless-edifier-w800bt-pro.review: A very good, balanced sound. Very quiet ANC. The earpads are a bit small, but the mic sounds really good, the ANC is really good, and it keeps getting more affordable. And it CAN RUN WIRED OVER USB-C, EXACTLY LIKE SENNHEISER'S TECH. Crazy, it's too cheap. (Full review on his YouTube: WH700NB Pro vs W800BT Pro vs W830NB.)

headphone-wireless-roseselsa-cambrian.review: Tough. No EQ. The default tonality is very midrange, with very little bass. The earpads are small. It still struggles to beat brands that have long made wireless products, like EarFun, Soundcore, SoundPeats and Tozo.

headphone-wireless-tozo-h100.review: No fuss if you want cheap. A good driver, not murky; not being muffled is a blessing already. This is good: slightly muddy in the low-mids, but my custom EQ is already in the app (filter by the headphone name "Tozo H100" in EQ Zone). Done. Don't expect a wide soundstage or imaging. Nothing competes at this price. The earpads are replaceable and sold directly by Tozo. Good mic.

headphone-wireless-soundcore-space-q45.review: Best at a million rupiah, with a very well-balanced sound. Soundcore is usually very V-shaped; these mids are good now. Enough sub-bass, not too much. Decent soundstage. Much cheaper than the Edifier WH950NB and Sony C720, but the quality is really good, I swear. The Edifier's volume is a bit low; this one isn't at all: it's loud without maxing out.

headphone-wireless-moondrop-edge.review: Hard to split the audience between ordinary wireless consumers and ChiFi brands. At this price, better the Edifier W830NB or Wave Pro: better app, USB-C wired mode, better warranty. The price isn't OK; overpriced. Looks lovely, good fit, surprisingly good ANC, OK tonality, ordinary technicalities. My strong advice remains: for wireless, don't go ChiFi yet.

headphone-wireless-soundpeats-space.review: A 123-hour battery, ANC, a low-latency mode, custom EQ. OK. Weakness: the earpads are a bit small. Better than the Q20i on low-latency mode and battery; sound and ANC nearly identical. I strongly recommend using ANC mode, because Normal and Transparency sound too neutral to me, not fun enough for most consumers. (Video review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-soundcore-q20i.review: Well balanced, with more sub-bass punch below 100 Hz. Already nice without fiddling, but with my custom EQ it becomes warmer with balanced low-mids. BEST. More punch and power than the Q45. Don't worry about the codec: even I can't tell LDAC from AAC on Apple Music/Spotify, let alone ordinary consumers. Works with a 3.5 mm jack, has ANC and transparency. KING OF BUDGET: BUDGET HEADPHONE OF THE YEAR.

headphone-wireless-edifier-wh700nb-pro.review: No custom EQ. A bit bright, neutral. Only with ANC on does the tuning change to bassier, adding sub/low end and cutting mid-bass. Only EQ presets: Classic and Pop are still a bit better, but at loud volume it'll sound very bright. (Full review on his YouTube: WH700NB Pro vs W800BT Pro vs W830NB.)

headphone-wireless-edifier-wh950nb.review: The bass is there, not over-punchy. Long battery. VERY GOOD mic, PARAMETRIC EQ, game mode, theatre mode. Cheap and already good. Almost no weaknesses; at most it's a little less loud with my custom EQ. Comes with a nice case. Good for office workers who can't afford a flagship yet. Silent ANC, no hiss. The Stax S3, by contrast, has no ANC and a weaker mic (read across to the right). This one's still bassy; the Stax is neutral.

headphone-wireless-sony-wh-ch720n.review: Light, good, comfortable and lightweight, with a metal insert in the headband. Top-class, natural ANC that doesn't change the music's sound in ANC mode. Shame it's still AAC, and the midrange, upper midrange and treble still aren't clear.

headphone-wireless-edifier-wh700nb.review: Codec stuck at SBC, while the W800BT Plus at the same price already has aptX. Yes, OK, it has ANC, but no custom EQ; far behind the Q20i on value. Neutral sound. And the main weakness of every Edifier headphone is LOW VOLUME, even with the phone and the headphone at maximum. Neutral sound with really very little bass; ordinary consumers who like bass surely won't like it. Just get the Q20i.

headphone-wireless-philips-tah2000.review: Much better than the JLab Rewind, guys: more bass, not thin and bright. It has a custom EQ too, and a good mic. Decent. The technicalities won't be like Koss, but at least the tuning will really satisfy bargain hunters. Comes with 2 extra earpads too. Louder than the JLab Rewind as well. (Video review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-jlab-rewind-2.review: OK for around 200k. Main weakness: the volume is a bit low on old masters, like non-remastered 80s and earlier songs. A bright tuning that can be EQ'd: still a bit bright, but friendlier. Swapping to Yaxi Koss-style earpads would probably warm it up. My EQ is in the table next door. A good mic for calls. Cheap. Adequate battery. (Video review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-edifier-w820nb-plus.review: The ANC is fairly natural, approaching the Sony CH720: good and natural. A neutral, less-bassy sound. It actually sounds nicer in ANC mode than in normal mode, which is a bit odd and should be fixable by firmware. In ANC, the Classic EQ is nice; in Normal, the Pop EQ. LDAC. I think the general public will prefer the W800BT Plus's sound; if you don't need ANC, that's more worth it. If your budget is bigger, just go for the Q45.

headphone-wireless-soundcore-h30i.review: On-ear, so it doesn't press on glasses. 70-hour battery, custom EQ, multipoint. It's the killer of every Baseus, Lenovo and Nokia. This Soundcore can't be beaten: the value is too high. Shut up and take my money!

headphone-wireless-sony-ch520.review: An on-ear shape, but comfortable because its tilt angle is very good. The sound is OK too, very balanced. This is really for when you want a different colour, worn around the neck as fashion, while getting good sound, a good mic and a custom EQ. On value it loses to the H30i: no multipoint yet, and a weaker battery. But if you want SONY, like its colours and don't like the Soundcore logo, up to you.

headphone-wireless-fantech-go-flow.review: The driver isn't bad, but there's no custom EQ yet, so the stock tuning has too much mids to low-mids: from 1 kHz down to 250 Hz it's fairly boosted. Maybe fine for casual listeners who don't notice, or you can EQ with a third-party app, though it won't be saved on the headphone. The driver definitely has good potential for a 300k budget. (Review on his YouTube.)

headphone-wireless-baseus-h2.review: I bought this myself. Such a waste, man. No LDAC/aptX. ANC is decent but still loses to the Edifier W820NB Plus. A mess at this budget, honestly. If you're spending this much, better buy the Q45, sir: LDAC, custom EQ. This thing only suits people who want AirPods Max-style prestige. The sound is safe, balanced, nothing amazing, but not piercing or too bassy either. The fit is OK too.
